title: Modeling Cryptocurrency Returns with Generalized Hyperbolic Distributions: Estimation, Diagnostics, and Model Comparison
content: Bitcoin and Ethereum exhibit distinct distributional characteristics that warrant asset-specific modeling. This study fits the five-parameter generalized hyperbolic (GH) distribution to daily returns for both cryptocurrencies using maximum likelihood estimation. The estimation procedure is evaluated through convergence analysis, score-function assessment, and verification of the Hessian eigenvalues. Based on the maximized log-likelihood, AIC, and BIC, the GH distribution substantially outperforms the Gaussian benchmark for both assets. The results indicate that Bitcoin returns are approximately symmetric, whereas Ethereum returns exhibit statistically significant positive asymmetry. The strictly negative Hessian eigenvalues confirm the negative definiteness of the Hessian at the estimated parameter vectors, providing numerical evidence that the estimates correspond to strict local maxima. These findings demonstrate the importance of accounting for heavy tails and asset-specific asymmetry, as Gaussian models may underestimate extreme risk, particularly in portfolio allocation and cryptocurrency risk management.
